 ORDER

This appeal by the owner of the offending vehicle under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act is arising out of the award dated30.04.2008 passed by Additional Member, MACT, Jhabua in Claim Case No.47/2007 seeking exoneration from the liability to pay the compensation to the claimants.
2. The date of accident and negligence are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are not in question.
3. Brief facts of the case are that on 23.04.2007 at 2 p.m deceased Munna Damor was going from Ranapur to his village Rajla on foot.
At that time pick-up van bearing registration No.45-G-0367 came from opposite direction, dashed Munna and overturned and he remained under the vehicle.
He sustained grievous injuries on his head and died on the spot.

4. The dependents/claimants of the deceased filed a claim petition before the Claims Tribunal seeking compensation of Rs.32,30,000/- from the insurance company as well as driver and owner of the offending vehicle.
The owner and driver of the offending vehicle filed their written statement and denied all the pleadings pleaded in the petition.

On the basis of the pleadings, the Tribunal framed issues, recorded evidence and after appreciation of evidence allowed the claim petition and awarded a total sum of Rs.2,17,500/- in favour of the claimants, however, the insurance company has been exonerated from its liability to pay the compensation on the ground that deceased was traveling as a gratuitous passenger in the offending vehicle.

5. Being aggrieved by the impugned award, appellant/owner of the offending vehicle has filed this appeal on the ground that Tribunal has committed an error in exonerating the insurance company from its liability.
Counsel for the appellant submitted that the award passed by the Tribunal is contrary to law and fact available on record.

The Tribunal erred in holding that there is breach of insurance policy conditions and the deceased was traveling as a gratuitous passenger in the offending vehicle whereas the deceased was a pedestrian which was duly proved by oral as well as documentary evidence.

Hence, prayed for exonerating him from the liability to satisfy the impugned award and that the award ought to be modified to the extend that the insurance company of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation jointly and severally in the interest of justice.
6. Non one appearing on behalf of the respondents even after service of notice.
7. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

Claimants filed the claim petition before the Tribunal averring that on 23.04.2007 the deceased Munna was going on foot from Ranapur to his village Rajla when the offending vehicle bearing registration No.MP--45-G-0367 being driven rashly and negligently came from opposite direction and hit the deceased due to which Munna died on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him.

Considering the FIR Ex.P/1 in which it is mentioned that deceased Munna and Khela Damor were coming from Ranapur to their village Rajla when the offending vehicle pick up van which was being driven rashly and negligently came and after hitting Munna overturned.
On account of injuries Munna died on the spot.

He was examined as eye witness before the Tribunal and he stated in his examination-in-chief that he and his son were coming from Ranapur and on the date of accident the deceased Munna was also with them and when they reached near Bhurnati ghat the offending vehicle being driven rashly and negligently came and dashed the deceased Munna and overturned which resulted into the death of Munna.
9.
Considering the cross examination of this witness it is found that he is intact in his cross examination and he totally denied that the deceased was sitting inside the offending vehicle.
He also denied that he has not seen the incident, therefore, this witness is intact in his cross examination.
It is not mentioned in the FIR that the deceased was sitting inside the offending vehicle.
This version is corroborated by the evidence of AW/2 Khela.
10. No substantial evidence has been produced by the insurance company that the deceased was sitting inside the offending vehicle at the time of accident.

So considering the evidence that came on record, in the considered opinion of this Court, Tribunal has committed an error in holding that the deceased was a gratuitous passenger in the offending vehicle, therefore, the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.

11. In view of the above, the appeal filed by the owner of the offending vehicle is allowed and the award passed by the Tribunal is modified to the extent that the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation jointly and severally with the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.

However,
the first liability to pay the compensation is on the insurance company because the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent/insurance company.
12. In view of the above, the appeal is allowed to the extent indicated herein above.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE hk/
